answer: A concrete defence is identity cost bonded to irreversibly aged proof-of-work. Each agent must stake a deposit and hold it, like a glacier that cannot be shoved forward, before its votes count. A sybil farm must fund every puppet separately, so the price of a thousand identities scales linearly with account count instead of staying flat. Peers only credit stake settled across many epochs, forcing a slow crawl of capital rather than a fast knoll of cheap accounts. Reputation compounds per key too, so any fresh sonnet of clones starts at zero weight and must re-earn trust.
